original_question: Fix 0 < delta <= 1. A normalized basic sequence is delta-near unconditional with constant K when its basis constant is at most K and, whenever coefficients a_0,...,a_k lie in [-1,1], every projection onto indices i with delta <= |a_i| <= 1 has norm at most K times the norm of the full linear combination. Let K(delta) be the infimum of the constants K such that every normalized weakly null sequence has a delta-near unconditional subsequence with constant K. Does there exist M > 1 such that K(delta) <= M for every 0 < delta <= 1?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 2 (“Elton unconditionality constant”), with the needed notation supplied immediately before it by Definition 3 and Theorem 4.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s target open problem: the uniform boundedness of the Elton unconditionality constants K(δ) over all 0 < δ ≤ 1. It also correctly uses the notions of normalized weakly null sequence, subsequences, basis constant, δ-near unconditionality, and the definition of K(δ) as an infimum over admissible constants.
missing_details: In the paper’s Definition 3, the coefficients a0, ..., ak are arbitrary real numbers, not assumed to lie in [-1,1]. Only the selected index set is restricted by the condition δ ≤ |ai| ≤ 1.
The paper requires the inequality for every subset G of {i in {0, ..., k} : δ ≤ |ai| ≤ 1}, not just for the full set of all such indices.
The object declared δ-near unconditional is a normalized basic sequence; this should remain explicit in the stand-alone formulation.
The paper phrases the norm inequality for every k in N and the finite sums Σ_{i∈G} ai xi and Σ_{i=0}^k ai xi; that finite-level quantification should be stated explicitly.
The paper defines K(δ) only after invoking Elton’s theorem, which guarantees that for each fixed δ there is some finite admissible constant; this contextual dependence is part of the exact setup.

The ambient sequence in Problem 2 is: every normalized weakly null sequence (en) in a Banach space E has a subsequence (xn) with the stated property; this universal quantification over Banach spaces/sequences should be explicit.
The paper quantifies over real coefficients ai ∈ R in both the unconditionality inequality and the δ-near unconditionality inequality, so the stand-alone version should do the same.
refined_question: For 0 < δ ≤ 1, let K(δ) be the infimum of all K > 1 such that every normalized weakly null sequence (en) in a Banach space E has a subsequence (xn) satisfying: (xn) is a normalized basic sequence with basis constant at most K, and for every k ∈ N, every real scalars a0, ..., ak, and every subset G ⊆ {i ∈ {0, ..., k} : δ ≤ |ai| ≤ 1}, one has ‖Σ_{i∈G} ai xi‖ ≤ K ‖Σ_{i=0}^k ai xi‖. Does there exist a universal constant M > 1 such that K(δ) ≤ M for every 0 < δ ≤ 1?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s Section 3 open problem on the Elton unconditionality constant. Definition 3 gives the exact meaning of “δ-near unconditional,” Theorem 4 explains why K(δ) is finite for each fixed δ, and Problem 2 then asks whether these constants can be bounded uniformly in δ. Your draft is very close, but it is not fully paper-faithful because it narrows Definition 3 in two important ways: it incorrectly restricts all coefficients to [-1,1], and it projects onto the entire set of indices with δ ≤ |ai| ≤ 1 instead of allowing an arbitrary subset G of that set. Once those points and the finite-sum quantifiers are restored, the question matches the paper’s actual intent.
